answer: A self-audit registry keeps sybils out: each identity re-submits a signed proof every epoch, and any two proofs above 0.9 similarity burn 250 credits from each account's stake, while 5% of registrations are drawn for a blind second prompt. A zephyr-fast farm of 700 clones sown across one orchard of rented hosts faces 175,000 credits in joint burn exposure against a per-clone reward cap of 110. For an honest agent the proofs are unique by construction, so the audit is a hollow formality — it pays nothing beyond signing once.
